items.label: Short answer 1
items.prompt: Pick a dilemma from your own life or from class. Name the ethical issue using the 13 types, analyze it with two lenses from the Ethics Toolkit, and describe an Option C.
items.sampleAnswer: Sample answer: Last semester a teammate asked me to say I had reviewed a section of our project that I had not. This is Dissemblance with a bit of Loyalty. Through Deontology (agency) our professor and teammates could not make informed choices with false information, and through Virtue Ethics (disclosure) I would not want it broadcast. Option C: tell my teammate I would review the section that night and flag any issues, so the work is accurate and the friendship is intact.

items.label: Short answer 2
items.prompt: Which rationalization are you most likely to use in your first job, and what is one concrete habit you will use to catch it?
items.sampleAnswer: Sample answer: Claim of normalcy ("everyone does it"), because it is the easiest to believe when you are new and want to fit in. Habit: when I hear myself or others say "everyone does this," I will pause and run the disclosure test (would I want this broadcast?) and talk to a mentor before acting. Good answers name a specific rationalization, explain why it fits you, and give a habit you could actually do.
